text:
maria.cs: @here quick sync on EnclaveCorp private deploy — their infra team pushed the VPC + peering but the runbook flagged three gaps: 1) NAT/subnet routing for inference nodes, 2) KMS key alias + key policy/grants for Redwood service role, 3) CloudTrail/audit logs forwarding to their SIEM. Can we triage?

devon.eng: :wave: I can own the subnet/routing piece. Which AZs and CIDR are they using?

maria.cs: They used 10.28.0.0/16 with 3 public and 3 private subnets. Inference pods will sit in the private subnets behind a NAT. Right now the private route tables only have the local route (10.28.0.0/16 -> local) — no 0.0.0.0/0 via NAT.

raj.netops: That's the main blocker for egress. Need a route to the NAT gateway and SGs allowing outbound 443 to our endpoints. Quick snippet I recommend: 

raj.netops: ```
# replace route to point to NAT GW
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc1234 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-0def5678
```

devon.eng: Also confirm DNS: they should have a private hosted zone or conditional forwarder so `api.redwood-inference.internal` resolves to our ENI. Are they doing cross-account Route53 resolver rules or using VPC peering + private hosted zone association?

leo.custops: On KMS — they created a CMK alias `alias/enclave-redwood` but omitted the key policy and grants. We need them to add the Redwood service role (arn:aws:iam::1234567890:role/redwood-service-role) with Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions, and allow CloudTrail to use the key for log delivery if S3 uses SSE-KMS.

leo.custops: Example command to push a policy or grant: 
```
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id 1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab --policy file://redwood-key-policy.json
# or grant for service role
aws kms create-grant --key-id 1234abcd... --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::1234567890:role/redwood-service-role --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey
```

sara.sec: For audit logs, ask them to forward CloudTrail to their `enclave-logs-prod` S3 and ensure the bucket policy allows CloudTrail and our log-lifecycle account (if applicable) to read objects. If S3 is SSE-KMS, the key must grant CloudTrail PutObject. Also confirm they aren't routing logs through a central aggregator that strips CloudTrail fields.

maria.cs: Can we turn this into a short runbook checklist to send to the customer? This is flagged as a potential renewal risk if cutover misses the Monday window — they expect traffic next week. We need clear owners + ETAs.

devon.eng: I'll own routing + DNS. ETA: EOD today for NAT route + private hosted zone validation.

raj.netops: I'll fix SGs and ensure outbound rules to 0.0.0.0/0:443 are present for inference subnets. Will also verify NAT gateway attachment. ETA: EOD.

leo.custops: I'll draft the key policy + sample create-grant commands and paste them here in the next hour.

sara.sec: I'll validate the CloudTrail->S3 pipeline and provide the S3 bucket policy checklist by 17:00 UTC. Tied up until 15:00 but will post updates after.

ops-bot: Reminder: scheduled cutover window Mon 09:00-11:00 UTC. Please update status if any blocker remains.

maria.cs: Thanks all — owners: devon (routing/DNS), raj (SGs/routes), leo (KMS), sara (audit). I'll consolidate the runbook and send to the customer PM. If anyone hits a blocker please @maria.cs and escalate. :thumbsup:
